summary.coverage: every row read through targeted risk sweeps (all 61 non-user-role rows, all 275 completes, all 158 reinstates, all 70 message_new_rule rows, all inactive-status rows, all hedged/quoted/single-reply/sub-unit/task-switch regex hits, all cancels-with-replacement and supersedes-without-replacement-cue hits, plus a 45-row random read).
systemic_findings: target_span.end is wrong on 1206/1466 rows (end != start + len(text)). Fix rule: end = start + len(text). Not itemised below.
target_span.start is wrong on 70/1466 rows (message[start:start+len(text)] != text; offsets are off by 1-9 chars). Fix rule: start = message.find(text), then end = start + len(text).

2 of those 70 spans are not verbatim substrings at all and need text normalisation, not just an offset fix: row idx 557 span 'Also attach...' vs message 'also attach...' (case), and row idx 724 span '"equations should never be numbered in working papers"' vs message '...working papers,"' (comma inside the closing quote).

1191/1466 rows use the whole message as the candidate span, so multi-clause messages (e.g. 'Stop numbering hypotheses..., and also date each memo header from now on.') are not sentence-split as the spec's splitter requires.
new_rule_spans emits two shapes: 62 bare strings and 9 span objects with offsets. The spec requires character offsets plus exact quotes; normalise to span objects.

Required identity fields are largely absent: id missing on 1426 rows, scenario_id on 1386, author/session_id on 770, split on 771. Without scenario_id the spec's scenario-level (not row-level) split cannot be enforced -- and rows 502/503 are a deliberate live/cancelled minimal pair on one message that MUST share a scenario group.

Row idx 625 carries status 'systematic' (not one of live/cancelled/completed/superseded); it is a task:'systematic review' rule and the intended status is clearly live. Label cancels is correct; fix the enum value.

No benchmark echo found: lexical scan of old_rule+message for every excluded evaluation family and for characteristic instruction-following markers returned 0 real hits (the single 'placeholder' hit, row idx 814, is an ordinary runbook rule). No file under data/bench and no gate bank under results/quick-checks/focus3-gate was opened.

No duplicates: 0 messages shared with kimi-relations/opus-enrich/astra-enrich(-2); the only repeated (old_rule, message, span) triple is 502/503, a deliberate status-only minimal pair, which is retained.
positive_findings: Status preconditions are clean: 0 supersedes/cancels/completes rows target an inactive version, and all 158 reinstates target cancelled/completed/superseded versions -- the dominant defect class of the earlier kimi-relations audit (50 rows) does not recur here.
All 61 non-user-role rows (31 tool, 30 assistant) are none with message_new_rule=false.
0 completes rows target a global-scope rule, and every completes message names the target rule's own task; the sub-unit-closure and task-switch negatives are correctly none (idx 197, 314, 119).
0 hedged/tentative messages and 0 quoted/reported messages carry a positive label.
ambiguities: Scoped suspension vs supersedes: idx 465 (global 'outline meals before shopping lists' + 'For the meal plans, stop outlining meals first -- just dive into the shopping list') is labelled cancels. The narrower phrase names essentially the rule's whole applicability and a replacement order is implied, so cancels/supersedes/none are all arguable; v3 settles bare narrower suspensions (none) but not one whose narrower scope equals the rule's entire domain.

Reinstate-with-replacement against a live version: idx 703 ('Go back to calling them subjects; replace participants in everything from now on') is supersedes because the visible target is the live rule and the message carries an explicit replacement span, while idx 960 ('reinstate the old lookup rule') is relabelled none under L2. The spec does not say which cue wins when a message is both a restoration and an explicit replacement; I applied 'explicit reinstate/original-version reference => L2 none, otherwise supersedes'.

User endorsement of a reported non-user action: idx 1334 ('The assistant already removed the screenshot size limit, so the audit should ignore it now') is none. 'should ignore it now' is user-authored deontic text, so this is arguably cancels; I kept none under the conservative-reading rule, but the spec does not cover a user ratifying an assistant's claimed change.

Key identity for near-domain narrower updates: idx 441 (global 'rank vacation spots by cost' vs 'For the team offsite, rank venues by accessibility instead') stays none as different subject matter, while idx 319/869 become supersedes as the same key. The conflict test is judgement-heavy exactly here; a worked pair in the spec would remove the guesswork.

message: Go back to using VLOOKUP; reinstate the old lookup rule.
old_rule: From now on use the XLOOKUP function instead of VLOOKUP.
why: L2/D:11: on a reinstating message ('reinstate the old lookup rule') the currently live same-key version receives none; its shadowing is derived by precedence from the restored version's later turn, not annotated as supersedes.

message: For the survey weighting memo, keep the profile as a paragraph instead of a numbered list.
old_rule: From now on deliver every dataset profile as a numbered list.
why: Narrower task update against a global rule of the SAME key with an explicit replacement value on an identifiable task (survey weighting memo) supersedes on the intersection (spec none-def sentence 3; v3 scoped-suspension clause). The corpus' own convention agrees (row 241, 'For the quarterly investor letter specifically...' vs a global subject-line cap = supersedes).

message: On the pricing workbook, colour overdue cells crimson instead.

why: Same as above: global 'colour overdue cells amber' vs 'On the pricing workbook, colour overdue cells crimson instead' is the same key (overdue-cell colour) with an explicit replacement value on an identifiable narrower task; supersedes on the overlap, global survives elsewhere.
